title: Phase 2b web A/B, Chrome 4x CPU throttle, old (5f7ecd8) vs new (HEAD + uncommitted Phase 2b)

env.browser: Google Chrome (system app, headless, via playwright-core)

commitNote: old = git archive 5f7ecd8 src; new = worktree HEAD plus uncommitted Phase 2b changes

method.harness: React hook path: real useMarkdownStream + <Markdown document> in react-native-web, one chunk per 16 ms on a real timer, fresh hook per run (not bench/stream-web.mjs, which simulates tail parse and cannot see the pacer or fade)
method.bundles: one harness bundled twice with esbuild (react-native aliased to react-native-web, production, __DEV__ false): old against the old src, new against the current src
method.session: one Chrome session, 4x CPU throttle via CDP Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate, old and new on separate pages, configs rotated each round, page reloaded per fixture block
method.runs: 2 warm-up (discarded) + 10 measured per config per fixture (the driver ran 12 rounds)

limits: the public hook exposes no flush cost: metrics are commit based
new-smooth and new-fade latency and total are not like for like with old (pacing adds up to about 0.2 s of drain after done())
a new-core none mode cannot be driven through the hook, so it is not covered
dropped (frame gap over 20 ms) and frameGapP90 are identical across configs: 4x throttle plus the 16 ms timer pacing saturate them, so they do not discriminate
harness scripts live in the job tmp dir, not in the repo
